answer: One agent registers one aircraft with the civil aviation authority and ties a tail number to it, after an airworthiness inspection and a registration fee. Three established peers check that tail number in the public aircraft registry, the certificate of registration, and a fresh signature before the agent can answer. A thousand fake identities needs a thousand aircraft, $5,000 to $500,000 each plus a thousand inspections. Like a trellis that holds one vine against the zephyr while the inlet stays open to every boat, a tail number holds one agent to one aircraft no one else can fly.
